title: split-phase-arbiter-low-latency-fairness-strategy
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Proposal and implementation track for a 'Split-Phase Arbiter' scheduler that enforces per-phase soft-quotas and low-latency guarantees while preserving long-term fairness. This ticket covers algorithm design, integration with kernel selection and attention-cost signals, performance microbenchmarks, and canary rollout plan. Goal: reduce p99 latency regressions under mixed workloads by up to 25% while keeping throughput within 10% of baseline and preventing starvation of long-running prefill jobs.
technical_summary: We introduce a two-stage arbitration: PhaseSplit (separates prefill vs decode windows per request) and WindowedSoftQuota (dynamically allocates tokens per phase based on a continuous fairness score). The arbiter consults: (1) model/kernel latency estimates, (2) live attention-cost telemetry (per-token attention FLOP proxy), and (3) per-request SLA hints. Scheduler outputs a route: immediate-decode, staged-prefill, or slow-path batch. Integrates hooks to kernel-selector to prefer lower-latency kernels for decode-critical slices.
design_decisions: Keep phase affinity: each request's tokens are tagged with phase IDs to allow KV cache reuse across split windows.
Use soft-quotas with decay instead of hard caps to avoid abrupt throughput collapse for heavy departments.
Prioritize latency-sensitive routes (api tier) during the decode sub-window; prefill-heavy background jobs get proportional share during prefill windows.
Expose a per-customer priority multiplier to the arbiter for Dedicated tenants.
Kernel selection integration: when decode window is scheduled, prefer kernels profiled for short sequence fast-step; fallback to throughput-optimized kernels outside decode-critical windows.
tradeoffs: Favoring decode-latency reduces instantaneous throughput due to shorter batch windows; soft-quotas mitigate long-term throughput loss but increase implementation complexity. Kernel preferring may cause slight model-accuracy differences on quantized kernels; we will validate quality via eval sets. Adding per-customer multipliers increases scheduling state and requires careful UX in Redwood Console.
proposal: Implement PhaseSplit + WindowedSoftQuota in scheduler v2. Steps: (1) lightweight simulator to validate policies on historical request traces; (2) implement arbiter and API toggles; (3) add kernel preference API; (4) run microbenchmarks and a 1% canary in hosted API; (5) ramp to fleet with telemetry-driven fallback thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator demonstrates >=15% reduction in p99 decode latency on mixed trace vs current baseline with <=10% throughput drop
No request class experiences starvation in 24h live-sim test (defined as >3x baseline tail latency)
End-to-end automated tests for phase-tag propagation and KV cache correctness
Kernel-selection hook correctly chooses low-latency kernels in 95% of decode-critical slices in canary
Console exposes 1 toggle to enable/disable Split-Phase Arbiter per deployment and documents cost implications
implementation_steps: Create deterministic scheduler simulator and replay infra (eng/bench) — Miguel
Design wire protocol for phase tags on request metadata and KV cache keys — Miguel + Priya
Add WindowedSoftQuota state storage (sharded counters with decay) and fairness scoring — Backend team
Kernel-selector: add preference flag and expose runtime profiling endpoint — Runtime team
Integrate telemetry: attention-cost proxy and per-token latency estimator — Observability
End-to-end tests and chaos scenarios (node failure, cache eviction) — SRE
Canary rollout: 1% -> 5% -> 20% with automated rollback on QPS/p99 breach — Platform
testing_plan: Unit tests for quota decay math and phase-tag propagation. Simulator validation against traces from last 30 days across three customer cohorts. Microbenchmarks on: short-decode-heavy chat, long-prefill summarization, and mixed synthetic workloads. Canary monitors: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, kernel-swap rate, cache-hit ratio, error rate. Automated rollback if p99 increases by >10% or error rate delta >0.5%.
monitoring_and_dashboards: New dashboard: SplitPhase/Realtime showing phase window occupancy, soft-quota budgets, and fairness score histogram
Alert: phase-budget-starvation if <5% of requests consume >60% of budget for 5m
Histogram: kernel-selection preference vs actual latency per-slice
Customer-facing cost dashboard update to show cost-per-token change when split-phase enabled
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated. Start internal canary on staging, then limited hosted customers (opt-in), then automatic canary in main cluster. Provide Dedicated customers a config option to pin behavior. Rollout stages tied to telemetry gates with guardrails. Post-rollout: 2-week observation window and retrospective.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: KV cache fragmentation due to phase-splitting -> Mitigation: tag TTL alignment and early coalescing logic
Risk: Kernel thrashing (frequent kernel swaps) -> Mitigation: minimum kernel-hold window and hysteresis
Risk: Unforeseen fairness regressions for background jobs -> Mitigation: offline fairness sim and adjustable decay constants, emergency admin override
Risk: Customer confusion about cost changes -> Mitigation: Console messaging and per-customer cost impact report before enabling
notes: Related work: tie-ins with quantization recommendations (Optimize) — evaluate accuracy drift
We should surface a sample policy template for common tradeoffs: low-latency-chat, high-throughput-batch, balanced
Consider ML-informed quota tuner in follow-up to adapt decay constants to workload patterns
